newsitem.title: CANADA: Placer happy Highlands won't sue.
newsitem.headline: Placer happy Highlands won't sue.

text.p: Placer Dome Inc said Tuesday it welcomed an announcement from Highlands Gold Ltd that Highlands will not proceed with any legal action against Placer's A$0.75 a share takeover bid.
Placer had threatened to drop its bid if Highlands went to court. It said it was providing more data to satisfy Highlands even though it did not feel it was legally obligated to do so.
"Although not required by law, Placer Dome was happy to release this extra information to shareholders," Placer Dome President and Chief Executive Officer John Willson said.
"While the offer has only been in the hands of Highlands shareholders for one day, Placer Dome is already processing acceptances from both institutional and retail investors."
"We are extremely pleased that Highlands shareholders now have the opportunity to consider and accept our offer."

Placer said conditions on the offer have been removed for all but Papua New Guinea residents and shareholders on the Papua New Guinea register who await Papua New Guinea Central Bank approval. Furthermore, the case settlement period has been reduced to five business days from 30 days.

Among the additional information, Placer said the offer will be made by a Singapore holding company. If it succeeds in acquiring all of Highlands, Placer said it plans to maintain its interest in the Porgera gold mine joint venture "although the ownership of that interest may be changed to facilitate repatriation of dividends."

Placer said it would review and possibly change Highlands' exploration program, consider the mine potential of its Nena and Ramu projects in Papua New Guinea, close some offices and possibly undertake other changes.
If it acquires less than all of Highlands, it plans to force a restructuring of the Highlands' board. Highlands has said Placer's offer is inadequate.

Also, Placer intends to undertake a general review "with a view to causing Highlands to focus on its existing assets and to maximise dividends to its shareholders, rather than conducting exploration at its current levels."
Placer said that as of December 2 it held 33 percent of Highlands directly and indirectly.

Separately Placer announced it completed the sale of US$300 million of junior subordinated securities to two United States underwriter syndicates for distribution in U.S. capital markets. It issued US$200 million of 8.625 percent securities due in the year 2045, and US$100 million of 8.500 percent securities due in 2045, priced to yield 8.585 percent The securities are redeemable at par after five and 10 years, respectively.
